items.subject: accountancy
items.independent_calculation: Common-size expense share = expense / revenue × 100. P: 600/800 × 100 = 75%. Q: 160/200 × 100 = 80%. P has the lower expense share.

option_review.A: Correct: P is 75% and Q is 80%, so P has the lower share.
option_review.B: Incorrect: compares absolute rupee expenses (₹600 versus ₹160) rather than shares of revenue; Q's share is actually higher.
option_review.C: Incorrect: reverses the two calculated percentages and the resulting comparison.
option_review.D: Incorrect: being below revenue does not make the shares equal; they are 75% and 80%.

items.full_explanation: Common-size profit-and-loss statements express expenses as a percentage of revenue from operations. P: 600 ÷ 800 × 100 = 75%; Q: 160 ÷ 200 × 100 = 80%. P has the lower expense share despite its larger absolute expenses.

claim_audit.exact_claim: Common-size profit-and-loss statements express expenses as a percentage of revenue from operations.
claim_audit.assessment: Expense divided by revenue is exactly the supplied common-size profit-and-loss basis.

items.independent_calculation: Marginal cost for the increase from 3 to 4 units = change in total cost / change in output = (₹49−₹44)/(4−3) = ₹5 per unit.

option_review.A: Incorrect: ₹4 is not the change in total cost; total cost rises by ₹5 for one additional unit.
option_review.B: Correct: the total-cost increase is ₹5 over one unit of output.
option_review.C: Incorrect: ₹6 does not equal the observed cost difference.
option_review.D: Incorrect: ₹8 does not equal the observed cost difference.

claim_audit.assessment: The supplied NCERT excerpt explicitly defines SMC as change in total cost per unit change in output.

items.independent_calculation: Total cost = fixed cost + variable cost. TC rises from ₹20+₹60=₹80 to ₹20+₹75=₹95. For one additional unit, SMC = (₹95−₹80)/(9−8) = ₹15 per unit; equivalently, fixed cost is unchanged so the ₹15 increase in variable cost is the total-cost increase.

option_review.A: Incorrect: ₹8.33 is close to an average variable-cost calculation (₹75/9), not marginal cost.
option_review.B: Incorrect: ₹10.55 does not equal the ₹15 increase in total cost for one extra unit.
option_review.C: Incorrect: ₹13 does not equal the ₹15 increase in variable/total cost for one extra unit.
option_review.D: Correct: with fixed cost unchanged, total cost rises by ₹15 for the one-unit output increase.

items.full_explanation: Marginal cost is total variable cost divided by output: ₹75 ÷ 9 = ₹8.33. The keyed answer is D, ₹15.

claim_audit.exact_claim: Marginal cost is total variable cost divided by output: ₹75 ÷ 9 = ₹8.33.
claim_audit.assessment: 75/9 approximately8.33 is arithmetic for total variable cost per unit, not deltaTC/deltaq. True arithmetic does not validate the false marginal-cost definition.
